name: SunCommon
old_description: SunCommon has been operating in Vermont since 2012 and in New York since 2002! As the most tenured local solar company in our regions, we’re deeply committed to these beautiful communities. We’re dedicated to this place just like you, which means we’re equally invested in creating stronger, more vibrant communities together for years to come.
about:
SunCommon is headquartered in Waterbury, Vermont, and has been operating in New York since 2002 and in Vermont since 2012. The company was founded in 2002 and is structured as a certified B Corporation and a benefit corporation, reflecting a mission-driven ownership model that balances profit with social and environmental impact.

The company provides full-service solar and energy storage installation for residential, commercial, agricultural, non-profit, and municipal customers. Its services cover roof-mounted and ground-mounted solar arrays, battery backup systems (including Tesla Powerwall), electric vehicle charger installation, and community solar array development. SunCommon manages the entire project lifecycle — planning, financing, permitting, design, engineering, and construction — and reports having served over 10,000 customers across its two-state territory.

SunCommon’s customer base spans homeowners, businesses, farms, non-profits, and municipalities in Vermont and New York. Specific examples include residential rooftop and ground-mount systems, commercial solar projects that qualify for additional incentives, farm installations described as a “no-brainer” by the company, and community solar arrays that allow multiple utility customers to share the output of a single one-acre array through group net metering.

The company says its distinguishing features are its status as the most tenured local solar provider in its regions, its certification as a B Corporation and benefit corporation, and its mission to accelerate the transition to solar power because “ensuring a habitable planet is the most important work of our lifetimes.” It also notes being named the reader’s choice for solar and batteries since 2016.
